**Finding submitted — deviation (high severity), preferred cure.**

- **Responsive clause:** § 12.4 (p0050) is the only competitive restriction binding Customer; § 13.4 is ordinary acceptable-use (reverse engineering, security, lawful use) and not a non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
- **Why it fails:** undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor"), worldwide territory, 24 months post-term, and no internal-development or acquisition carve-out — walk-away territory, and it fails all five fallback elements.
- **Internal conflict noted:** § 12.3 (p0049) expressly records that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."
- **Redline (validated, ok:true, minimal):** surgical replace of the prohibitory operator and duration only — "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not" → "Customer may" — leaving the balance of the sentence verbatim, so § 12.4 now conforms to § 12.3 with no dangling references.
- **Element coverage:** the single preferred element is addressed by operation 1; the comment offers the narrowed fallback as a negotiating position.
